function: Joint selection of MR-IoT association, BS receive-beam codebook index, MR transmit power and computation frequency to maximise computation efficiency; the beam is one of four learned decisions (pp. 8-9).
system: Multi-antenna BS (N antennas, number not stated), 8 single-antenna MRs and 5 single-antenna IoT backscatter devices; uplink, 2.6 GHz, 2 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Distributed multi-agent DRL: fingerprint-based dueling double DQN (FD4QN), one DQN agent per MR at the BS, independent Q-learning, offline training (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: multipath Rayleigh fading with ULA steering vectors, Gauss-Markov outdated CSI with Jakes model, path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d) (pp. 4-5, 11).
test_conditions: Offline training in the simulated HSR environment; results swept over train speed (240-480 km/h), data size, slot length and IoT distance; no separate unseen-scenario test stated (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Learned: D4QN (no fingerprint), DDQN with fingerprint; hybrids with nearest-IoT association or maximal power/frequency; non-learned: random scheme, exhaustive search (p. 12).
metrics: Total computation efficiency of all MRs (bits/J), reward per episode, CE gain with versus without SR (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Big-O training complexity O(M Nepi Nstep B w(8 Om1 + sum Omj-1 Omj + |A| OmJ)); count of weights given by the same sum (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "Rayleigh fading vector" - custom multipath simulator with ULA steering vectors and Gauss-Markov outdated CSI; p. 11 gives only a path-loss formula; no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "Total CE of all MRs against the train speed under different schemes" - each sweep (speed, data size, slot length, distance) is a separate setting; no model trained on one setting is stated to be tested on another, and training is offline from random initialisation (p. 10).
q3_support: p. 12: "based on the DDQN method (including fingerprint-based state setting)" - the learned baselines are D4QN (FD4QN without fingerprint) and DDQN with fingerprint (FD4QN without dueling), variants of the proposed method; the other schemes are hybrids using FD4QN, a random scheme and exhaustive search; no earlier published learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the total number of weights to be updated is" 8*Om1 + sum Omj-1*Omj + |A|*OmJ, and the training complexity is given as O(M Nepi Nstep B w(...)).
q5_support: p. 12: "All simulations are carried out on a PC with" - own Python and TensorFlow simulator with parameters in Tables II and III (p. 11); no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Borderline for the reviewer: the main objective is computation efficiency of MEC offloading; the DQN action jointly selects association, BS receive-beam index (Qcod = 4), MR power and CPU frequency (pp. 8-9), so area 3 by the beam decision and above_phy passes under the joint-decision clause. q3: DDQN includes the fingerprint state and D4QN drops it, so both are variants of FD4QN. The number of BS antennas N is not given numerically.
